evals.prompt: I run a small web design agency (sites are $4k one-time, usually $150/mo hosting after). I want to start cold emailing local med spas and dental clinics in Texas to get more clients. It's just me sending for now, maybe 30 emails a day. I've never done cold outreach before. Can you set me up with everything I need?
evals.expected_output: A complete campaign document: list plan (likely manual/community + a scraper test), 5-10 hooks, full cold email, follow-up cadence with copy for every touch, scaling plan, metrics, compliance (CAN-SPAM). Should NOT need to ask many questions since offer, ICP, channel, and capacity are given — but should ask about or state assumptions for lead magnet and proof points.
assertions: Asks about or explicitly assumes a lead magnet / free-value offer before or within the deliverable
Includes at least 5 distinct hooks/subject lines spanning different hook types
Includes a complete first-touch cold email under half a page with a personalization merge field
Includes a dated follow-up sequence with 6+ touches and actual copy for each touch, including a breakup email
Includes a list-building plan that references testing a sample before scaling
Includes metrics/benchmarks and a CAN-SPAM-relevant compliance note
Copy avoids banned phrases like 'I hope this email finds you well' and 'I wanted to reach out'

evals.prompt: write me a cold DM i can send to fitness coaches on instagram to sell my $997 course on getting more clients
evals.expected_output: Asks the load-bearing intake questions (proof, lead magnet, what the course delivers) OR states assumptions, delivers a 2-3 sentence DM at a low reading level with personalization, then offers/includes the surrounding follow-up sequence rather than a lone message.
assertions: The DM is 3 sentences or fewer
The DM contains a personalization element, not just {{first_name}}
The DM leads with value (a free gift/result) rather than pitching the $997 course directly
The response asks intake questions or explicitly lists its assumptions
The response offers or includes follow-up touches beyond the single DM

evals.prompt: I'm a bookkeeper, $400/mo per client, targeting owner-operated construction companies (5-30 employees) in Ohio. I want to do cold outreach on LinkedIn and email but honestly I have no idea what I could offer for free that anyone would care about. Where do I even start?
evals.expected_output: Runs the lead magnet generator: produces 5+ candidates across the three magnet types (reveal-the-problem audit, free sample of the service, one-step tool/template), scores them on the rubric table, recommends 1-2 with reasoning, pairs them with attention triggers relevant to construction companies, then delivers the full end-to-end campaign for LinkedIn + email.
assertions: Generates at least 5 lead magnet candidates spanning all three types (reveal-the-problem, free sample, one-step-of-many)
Presents a scoring table/rubric comparing candidates rather than just picking one
Recommends a specific magnet with a value anchor (what others charge for it)
Pairs magnets with attention triggers (why-now signals or observable gaps) specific to construction companies
Still delivers the complete sequence (hooks, copy for both channels, dated follow-ups), not just the magnet brainstorm

evals.prompt: Our SaaS ($500/mo, inventory management for e-commerce brands doing $1-10M) has an SDR team of 3 doing calls and emails into the US and Germany. Reply rates dropped from 4% to under 1% this quarter. Build us a new sequence and tell us what to test.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses likely causes using the funnel diagnostic (deliverability vs copy vs list fatigue), asks for or assumes missing metrics (open rate, bounce rate), delivers a new multi-channel sequence with hooks and copy, an A/B testing protocol (one variable at a time, ~200 sends per arm), and GDPR guidance for the German segment.
assertions: Uses funnel metrics (opens/bounces/replies) to diagnose or asks for them before/while prescribing
Delivers a multi-channel cadence using both email and phone since an SDR team exists
Includes an explicit A/B testing protocol with one-variable-at-a-time guidance
Addresses GDPR/legitimate interest for the Germany segment specifically
Provides new hooks/copy, not just strategy advice
